analyst_view.overall: Celta Fortuna (17th, 13 points, one win in ten) host Real Valladolid (13th, 18 points, six points off the play-offs) at Balaídos, a match both sides need; reports have said coach Fredi Álvarez is under pressure. Celta's reserve side plays fast, open football but leaks goals; they get centre-backs Joel López and Ribes back from bans, Hugo Cuenca is doubtful after returning from Paraguay duty with discomfort, and it is unclear whether the first team releases Andrés Antañón; Gavián, Somuah and Mateo Sobral are out (in the numbers). Valladolid miss Ojeda (banned) and Latasa (in the numbers) and right-back Trilli (adductor injury, not in the numbers), with Alejo back from a ban to replace him; Fran Escribá, back at the ground where he saved Celta in 2019, wants a serious game without end-to-end play. The EFE preview names José Antonio Sánchez of the Andalusian committee as referee; he is not yet in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already boosting Valladolid for 14 goals in their last six and trimming them for Latasa and Ojeda. I lean slightly lower to about 2.6 because Escribá again asked for a controlled game behind the ball, and Celta get two first-choice centre-backs, Joel López and Ribes, back from bans; Celta's leaky record keeps the size small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already add for Valladolid's recent corners (39 in six) against a Celta side that conceded 47. Trilli's absence takes away one of Valladolid's attacking full-backs, but Alejo is a like-for-like replacement, so nothing points either way and I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.5 cards, raised for Celta's recent card count, but they were made before the referee was named. If, as seems likely, this is José Antonio Sánchez Villalobos, he has averaged about 7 cards in the Segunda games we have on record with him (eight in Girona v Castellón this season), so I lift it a little to about 6.8; the sample is small, and Escribá's complaint about protest cards may calm Valladolid, which keeps the size modest.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, already lifted for Valladolid's recent shooting (88 in six) and Celta's openness. Escribá's caution points slightly down, Celta's young, fast side slightly up, and Cuenca's doubt and Antañón's uncertain release are too small to move it, so I stay at 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, boosted for Valladolid's 39 on target in their last six. Valladolid's expected front line of Víctor Fernández and Arnu with Abed and Ponceau behind is unchanged and Cabanzón starts on the bench, while Celta keep Álvaro Marín (8 goals), so nothing new points either way and I stay at 9.8.
